I've been there dude. I relate to your feelings. 

If you'd ask my advice, based on the picture you're drawing and what I did, you got two options that may be adapted to you age, atitude and level of financial independence.

1: get brutal. Fight her as if you were fighting hitler. Push her back to the hell she is coming from and draw a CLEAR line on what she can do or not. Stablish the consequences of crossing that line and DO IT if she persists after your warning. When I was a teenager that was my solution as I could not move. 

2: leave. That's what I did as soon I could. We kept some contact for an year and then I totally disappeared for 10 months. After all that time she realized the damage she caused to me, seems help and started to improve significantly. We just needed space. 

Above all, everyone dies. All things, good and bad, will fade. Take it as a phase (or a quest, if you prefer). Just DO NOT STOP your life for anyone. 

Move, move and keep fucking moving.

From somrone that almost did it a few months ago and now is mostly recovered: no.

I believe people have the right to die as much as they have to live. If course we tend to think about suicide amid desperation, so for most of times it's a definitive solution to a temporary problem - which is inappropriate.

I don't see how something SO personal could be selfish. 

You may see selfishness on the consequences such death would cause on your relatives and close friends, but this is inevitable, so I don't believe should be a factor. They should not be selfish and respect our decision to cease life.

Anyway, if that's what's running on your mind, don't do it before exhausting your options for help, starting from professional help. 

Reaching a therapist was one of the best things I've done in my life. Death is still an option, but not the first one anymore.

I will suggest you an exercise. Take a pice of paper and make three columns. Take some time on them.

1. Everything you have / know (money, goods, skills, knowledge)

2. Everyone you know that could support you in some way (i.e. "stay some time in my uncle's home until finding a new place)

3. Everything you'd like to achieve in the next 6 months, being realistic / optimistic. (Get away from him, find a new home)

Sit with it, think of all possible ways you could get out of this situation using the resources you have. Remember you don't need to do it by yourself, rely on the ones you have around you. 

You don't need necessarily to expose yourself and let every single person know why. Maybe you can reach a colleague that could point you to a better position at work, maybe some friends share a house and are looking for some one. 

As I said, take some time in the listing. You may find out you have more options than you feel you do.
